new_packages.label: תּוֹרָה, מִדּוֹת, וְיָמִים — שָׁלוֹשׁ בְּחִינוֹת אַחַת
new_packages.label_en: Torah, Midot, and Days — Three Aspects of One Reality

bechina_evidence.statement: הַיָּמִים נִקְרָאִים מִדּוֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: וּמִדַּת יָמַי
bechina_evidence.translation: The days are called midot, as it says: 'and the measure of my days'

bechina_evidence.statement: וְהַמִּדּוֹת הֵם הַתּוֹרָה, כִּי אוֹרַיְתָא כֻּלָּהּ הֵם מִדּוֹתָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ-בָּרוּךְ-הוּא
bechina_evidence.translation: And the midot ARE the Torah, for the entire Torah is God's midot
The Torah, that is to say the midot, that is to say the days

new_packages.reason: The source text contains a triple bechina equation that appears twice with explicit equating language. In section ג (line 10-11): days are 'called' midot (נקראים), and midot ARE the Torah (הם). In section ד (line 23): Torah = midot = yamim in a single triple heynu statement. These three concepts — תורה (Torah), מידות (the divine qualities/attributes), and ימים (days) — all share the same essential nature: they are all expressions of God's inner self as it radiates into the world in measured, contracted form. The Torah IS the midot because the whole Torah speaks of love, fear, and other qualities. The days ARE the midot because each day is a different quality-expression (Psalm 39: 'וּמִדַּת יָמַי'). None of these produce the other — they are three linguistic/conceptual faces of the same underlying reality: God's self-expression in contracted form. This cluster is entirely absent from the dataset for Torah #33.
new_packages.structural_role: This package is the structural 'field' of Torah #33. The entire teaching operates within this triple identity: the world of Torah/midot/yamim is the field where the holy ahavah is embedded. Package 1 (da'at/chesed) is the inward source; Package 2 (Torah/midot/yamim) is the medium through which that inner love is expressed. The teaching's argument is: through the days (which are midot which are Torah), God's ahavah is embedded — and through subduing the yetzer, one strips away the klipot-garments to reveal the Torah's letters and access that ahavah. Package 2 is the ontological background against which the entire teaching operates.
new_packages.confidence: HIGH — two separate triple-equation statements use unambiguous bechina language: 'נִקְרָאִים' (are called), 'הֵם' (are), and 'הַיְנוּ' (that is to say). Three nodes meet the 3-node threshold. They form a coherent independent domain (the manifestation-field of Divinity) distinct from Package 1 (the inner da'at/chesed source).

bechina_evidence.statement: הַתּוֹרָה נִקְרָא טוֹב, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: כִּי לֶקַח טוֹב נָתַתִּי לָכֶם

bechina_evidence.translation: Torah is called or (light), as it says: 'and Torah is light'

bechina_evidence.translation: Tzaddik is called tov (good), as it says: 'Say of the tzaddik: he is good'

bechina_evidence.statement: צַדִּיק נִקְרָא... אוֹר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: אוֹר זָרוּעַ לַצַּדִּיק
bechina_evidence.translation: Tzaddik is called or (light), as it says: 'light is sown for the tzaddik'

new_packages.reason: The source text (section ה, lines 34-35) contains four explicit bechina declarations. Torah is called 'tov' (good) — citing Proverbs 4:2. Torah is called 'or' (light) — citing Proverbs 6. Tzaddik is called 'tov' — citing Isaiah 3:10. Tzaddik is called 'or' (light) — citing Psalm 97:11. The text then draws the explicit conclusion (line 36): 'וּכְשֶׁיִּתְגַּלּוּ הַצַּדִּיקִים הַצְּפוּנִים וְהַתּוֹרָה הַצְּפוּנָה' — the hidden tzaddikim and the hidden Torah are revealed together, as one. The four nodes — Torah, tzaddik, tov (good), and or (light) — all share the same essential nature: they are all hidden realities ('אוֹר גָּנוּז' — the primordial hidden light) that share the quality of being both 'good' and 'light' in their concealed state, awaiting revelation in the future. The fact that both Torah and tzaddik are separately declared to BE tov and to BE or makes tov and or the shared bechina-bridge between them. These are not causes of one another — Torah does not produce tzaddikim here, nor vice versa. Both are independently declared to be the same thing: hidden good and hidden light.
new_packages.structural_role: This package represents the hidden/future dimension of the teaching. The entire Torah (sections ד-ה) builds toward the revelation of the hidden Torah and hidden tzaddikim at the end of days ('לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא'). The Torah Pnimit (inner Torah) and the tzaddikim who embody it are both described as hidden light awaiting revelation — the same 'or ki tov' from Genesis 1:4 that was stored away. This cluster is the eschatological/messianic dimension: the good-and-light that is currently concealed will be revealed as the ahavah-she-b'da'at floods the world.
new_packages.confidence: HIGH — all four bechina statements use the same 'נִקְרָא' (is called) formula. Four nodes meet the 3-node threshold easily. They form a coherent independent domain (hidden-good-light) distinct from Package 1 (inner da'at/chesed source) and Package 2 (Torah/midot/yamim as the ontological field).

observations:
Torah #33 is one of the most richly conceptual teachings in Likutay Moharan, yet it has only 2 bechina edges in the current dataset — making it the most under-encoded Torah analyzed so far. The source text contains at least 12 distinct bechina-language statements that are missing from the dataset entirely.

The teaching's structure can be understood as three concentric circles:

1. INNER CORE (Package 1 — da'at/chesed): The hidden ahavah that God has for Israel, which exists at a level above time and midot. This is the 'ahavah-she-b'da'at' — love as it exists in the Divine Mind before creation. Its nodes: דעת, חיים, חסד, כהן, אהבה.

2. MANIFESTATION FIELD (Proposed Package 2 — Torah/midot/yamim): The medium through which the inner love is expressed and contracted into time. Torah IS midot IS yamim — three faces of the same divine self-expression. This is where the Torah's letters (otiyot) are embedded, even within the klipot.

3. HIDDEN FUTURE (Proposed Package 3 — Torah/tzaddik/tov/or): The concealed dimension that will be revealed at the end of days. Torah and tzaddik share the same bechina of hidden-good-hidden-light. The 'ohr ki tov' of Genesis was stored ('לִגְנֹז') for the future — this is the same as the hidden tzaddikim and the inner Torah ('orayta de-atika stimaa').

The good/evil mirror: This Torah has a strong implicit evil-side that is not captured in the dataset at all. The 'ימי רע' (evil days), 'מידות רעות' (evil qualities), 'לשונות העכו"ם' (gentile languages), 'קליפות' (husks), and 'יצר הרע' (evil inclination) are all present throughout the text as the opposing force. These form an evil mirror package that is completely absent from the dataset for Torah #33.

Note on shared nodes: 'תורה' appears in both proposed Package 2 (as one of the Torah/midot/yamim triple) and proposed Package 3 (as what is called 'tov' and 'or'). Within Torah #33, these are distinct conceptual functions: in Package 2, Torah is the manifestation-medium (the field containing the otiyot); in Package 3, Torah is the hidden-good-light awaiting revelation. If both packages are accepted, the node 'תורה' would need to be split or assigned to the package where its bechina function is most dominant in Torah #33. Given that the Package 2 triple-equation (Torah = midot = yamim) is more structurally central to the teaching's argument, Torah should primarily sit in Package 2, with its 'tov/or' characterization noted as an additional bechina connection to Package 3.
